the problem of automatic melanoma detection in non-dermatoscopic images.
the development of a novel segmentation and learning algorithm to improve the diagnosis of melanoma from non-dermoscopy images.

a novel segmentation and ensemble algorithm were developed and used in conjunction to achieve a significant improvement in melanoma diagnosis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presented research demonstrates the ability to train deep learning algorithms on limited data, and the ability to accurately segment and quantify non-dermoscopically acquired lesion images.
we have developed a novel segmentation algorithm and a novel training algorithm that can be used in conjunction with each other or independently to improve automatic melanoma diagnosis.
our proposed methods, SCIDOG and the PECK ensemble algorithm, can learn well from limited training data and can be used to diagnose melanoma and benign nevi with high accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
limited data is not a barrier to achieving state-of-the-art performance on medical imaging tasks.
limited training data does not need to be a limitation for deep learning algorithms.
deep learning algorithms do not necessarily require thousands of images for successful generalization.
